description: Two ways of keeping a password that are not keeping a password safely, and they are different weaknesses with different remedies. Encoding is not hiding: base64 turns straight back into what went in. Encryption is not hashing: it is recoverable by design, which is the entire point of it and exactly what a stored password must never be. The hashed route is the negative, and the hash ends the classification everywhere rather than just here, because a password hash is not a password in any context.

expected.note: whoever holds the encoded form holds the password
recoverable by anyone who reaches the key
